draft.title: Manicouagan Reservoir – The Eye of Quebec

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find something strange in central Quebec.
A giant circular lake, about seventy kilometers across, looks like a huge eye from space.
The whole crater spans roughly one hundred kilometers, with the inner water ring at seventy kilometers.
What could have carved such a massive ring so perfectly?
A meteorite struck here about two hundred fourteen million years ago.
The impactor was about five kilometers in diameter, then the walls collapsed into a multi-ring basin.
Later the basin filled with water, forming the annular lake that hides René-Levasseur Island.
So that eye you saw is really a giant ancient impact scar.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

draft.description: Manicouagan Reservoir is an annular lake in central Quebec covering about one thousand nine hundred forty two square kilometers. It formed from a meteorite impact two hundred fourteen million years ago, leaving a crater about one hundred kilometers across.
